articles.title: He bought a Rs 41.85 lakh and paid Rs 39.15 lakh but did not get possession; builder blames PMC-PMRDA jurisdiction changes, MahaRERA rejects excuse and orders interest payout to homebuyer
articles.summary: When buying your dream home, timely possession is an important point.
articles.body: When buying your dream home, timely possession is an important point. Yet in some cases builders fail to deliver flats and houses within the stipulated time period.In one such recent case, the Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority (MahaRERA) has ruled that a builder cannot escape responsibility for delaying possession of flats by blaming administrative changes involving government authorities when the delay stems from its own failure.What the case is aboutA man bought a flat from a builder but did not get possession of it in the promised time period in the sale agreement.The builder, on its part, claimed that the delay was due to changes in government jurisdiction. The builder argued that, during 2022-2023, planning authority over Wagholi, where the project is located, shifted between the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) and the Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (PMRDA).Also Read | Woman buys Rs 1.03 crore 3BHK in Bengaluru, but builder fails to provide specially-enabled parking; Karnataka RERA orders provision within 60 days and audited maintenance accountsAccording to the builder, this change led to revised plans and fresh approvals, which held up the construction.The homebuyer, however, challenged this explanation before the MahaRERA tribunal by filing a rejoinder. He submitted documents to argue that the builder already knew Wagholi fell under PMC's jurisdiction before the sale agreement was executed.The homebuyer relied on a notification issued by the Urban Development Department (UDD) on June 30, 2021, which clearly placed Wagholi under PMC's jurisdiction.The homebuyer also pointed out that the plans for Wing C of the project, in which he had purchased a flat, had been approved by the RERA authority in January 2022. The sale agreement was then signed in September 2022, with possession scheduled for December 2024.The homebuyer alleged that the builder had invoked the PMRDA-PMC jurisdiction dispute only after the delay happened, using it as an excuse to explain why the flat had not been handed over to the buyer on time.Defending its position before the MahaRERA tribunal, the builder said it had offered compensation of Rs 35,000 as a goodwill gesture, without accepting liability for any inconvenience caused to the homebuyer.Also Read | Man invested Rs 10 lakh, which tax department treated as unexplained; he first cited cash loan, then bank withdrawals as source, ITAT Nagpur deletes addition and Rs 2.11 lakh penaltyWhy did the homebuyer win the case?In an order dated September 8, 2026, MahaRERA directed the developer to pay interest from January 1, 2025, until it hands over possession with the required Occupancy Certificate.The Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority (MahaRERA) rejected the builder’s explanation that changes involving the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) and Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (PMRDA) had held up approvals for its Wagholi project.The buyer relied on a June 30, 2021 notification from the state Urban Development Department that placed Wagholi under PMC’s jurisdiction.The authority did not accept the builder’s explanation as adequate justification for missing the agreed deadline. Securing approvals and obtaining the certificates required for a lawful handover remained the developer’s responsibility. It also needed credible evidence linking the administrative difficulties it cited to the delay.Also Read | Grandmother and her son gifted 2.5-acre land to his second wife, who sold it; his daughter from first marriage claimed it was ancestral, but Madras HC rejects her pleaThe builder had offered Rs 35,000 as a goodwill gesture, without admitting liability. That offer did not settle the matter. Under Section 18 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, a homebuyer can seek relief when a promoter fails to meet its obligations relating to completion or possession. MahaRERA held the developer liable under this provision.Aradhana Bhansali, Senior Partner at Rajani Associates, told ET that the buyer had succeeded because possession was not delivered within the timeline set out in the registered Agreement for Sale.The flat was priced at Rs 41.85 lakh, and the buyer had paid Rs 39.15 lakh. The remaining amount can be adjusted against the interest payable by the developer. The interest rate specified in the order is SBI’s marginal cost of funds-based lending rate (MCLR) plus 2%.The interest liability continues until the developer hands over the flat with the required Occupancy Certificate.Also Read | Man enters JDA for land, gets 6 flats from builder and transfers 5 to wife, but gets tax notice; ITAT Delhi deletes Rs 4.14 crore additions after finding no stock-in-trade conversion or saleYou use AI every day. articles.title: Rupee relief, higher hedging costs: What RBI’s new forex rules mean
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) latest measures to curb volatility in the rupee could ease near-term depreciation pressure, reduce
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) latest measures to curb volatility in the rupee could ease near-term depreciation pressure, reduce speculative dollar demand and help withdraw surplus liquidity from the banking system, according to research reports cited by news agency PTI.The measures, announced through circulars on October 10, include tighter restrictions on certain foreign exchange derivative transactions and a new reserve requirement for banks handling rupee-linked currency contracts.They are expected to make some hedging transactions more expensive, potentially reducing demand for dollars in the spot market and easing forward premiums.Kotak Mahindra Bank said the immediate impact on the rupee could be favourable, although it cautioned that the global environment remained uncertain."The immediate reaction on INR is expected to be very favourable-likely move of USDINR towards sub-95 cannot be ruled out. Forward premia is likely to soften as OMCs and other importer hedging gets contained," the bank said in its report.IDFC FIRST Bank also expects the measures to lower the USD/INR exchange rate and forward premiums in the near term, while noting that global conditions and balance-of-payments dynamics will shape the currency's medium-term trajectory.RBI tightens rules on forex derivativesUnder the October 10 circulars, the RBI barred authorised dealers from allowing users to rebook cancelled rupee-linked foreign exchange derivative contracts. Rollovers at maturity remain permitted, subject to existing regulations.The central bank also lowered the threshold for undertaking foreign exchange derivative transactions without establishing an underlying exposure to $5 million from $100 million. The revised limit applies across authorised dealers and recognised stock exchanges.In another measure, the RBI introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR). Authorised dealers must maintain the reserve with the central bank in cash, amounting to 20 per cent of the rupee equivalent of the notional value of each rupee-linked foreign exchange derivative contract exceeding $2 million, where the transaction hedges current account exposure involving the purchase of foreign currency against the rupee.The RBI said the measures were intended to strengthen market discipline, ensure appropriate risk management and maintain an orderly and transparent foreign exchange market.Higher hedging costs could curb dollar demandThe new reserve requirement could raise the cost of hedging currency exposure for importers, potentially discouraging some transactions and reducing demand for dollars.Kotak Mahindra Bank estimates that hedging costs could rise by 1-1.6 per cent, while IDFC FIRST Bank expects an increase of around 1.5 per cent.However, the relief to the rupee could be limited if external pressures persist. IDFC FIRST Bank identified elevated crude oil prices, foreign portfolio outflows and weak underlying capital flows as factors that could continue to weigh on the currency.The measures could also influence the RBI's interest-rate decisions. IDFC FIRST Bank said that if the steps ease depreciation pressure by curbing speculative demand and changing hedging behaviour, the central bank could adopt a gradual approach to further rate increases.The bank expects the terminal repo rate to be in the range of 6-6.25 per cent. The RBI raised the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October monetary policy meeting and shifted its stance to calibrated tightening.Banks expect further withdrawal of liquidityThe RBI's foreign exchange measures could also contribute to a reduction in surplus liquidity in the banking system.IDFC FIRST Bank estimates that core liquidity surplus could decline to around Rs 2 lakh crore by March 2027 from Rs 10.4 lakh crore on October 2, as currency leakage and balance-of-payments pressures add to the impact of the central bank's liquidity operations.Kotak Mahindra Bank estimates that the measures could withdraw around Rs 1.5 lakh crore of durable liquidity if they remain in force for another month. The bank also expects further liquidity withdrawal through open market bond sales and foreign exchange intervention.The RBI has announced an open market sale of government securities worth Rs 25,000 crore for October, following earlier liquidity-draining operations.It has also increased the daily maintenance requirement for the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) to 99 per cent from 90 per cent following a review of liquidity conditions.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: After failing to attract bidders for the ambitious Outer Harbour Container Terminal project at Tamil Nadu’s V O Chidambaranar (VOC) Port for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: After failing to attract bidders for the ambitious Outer Harbour Container Terminal project at Tamil Nadu’s V O Chidambaranar (VOC) Port for over two years, the Centre has decided to restructure the project by splitting it into two parts, making the port authority responsible for building the core infrastructure.The revised proposal with an estimated Rs 17,000 crore cost was taken up by the Union Cabinet last week, TOI has learnt. PM Narendra Modi had laid the foundation stone for the project in Feb 2024, with the expansion aimed at transforming VOC Port into a major transshipment hub on India’s east coast.Once completed, the port will be capable of handling ultra-large container vessels of up to 24,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) requiring an 18-metre draft. Such ships are over 400 metres long — roughly the length of four football fields.The project was originally approved on a design, build, finance, operate and transfer (DBFOT) model in 2024 — a first such pure public-private partnership in which the concessionaire was to build the entire facility and operate it at an estimated cost of around Rs 7,000 crore. It was designed to handle vessels of up to 18,000 TEUs with a 16-metre draft. Traditionally, port authorities build common infrastructure while private operators invest in equipment and run terminals.The port floated tenders twice, but prospective bidders flagged the project as financially unviable because of the high upfront investment required.Now under the revised structure, common civil infrastructure will be developed by the port authority through the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) at an estimated cost of Rs 11,700 crore. Private concessionaires will invest about Rs 5,400 crore in mechanisation, terminal operations and other development works.Officials familiar with the proposal said the restructuring also enhances capacity. While the original plan envisaged two terminals with a combined capacity of 4 million TEUs, the revised proposal increases this to 5.2 million TEUs.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Is 8% next? Why mortgage rates have surged, and may stay higher for longer
articles.summary: Strong economic growth, high oil prices, and a rush of AI spending mean mortgage rates may be stuck at high levels.
articles.body:
Mortgage rates are on a rough ride. In just over a month, they're up a full percentage point to around 7.5%, a three-year high . Buyers are pulling back in response, and September home sales look poised for a steep downturn.

How did this happen ? Blame surging bond yields worldwide. Mortgage rates are particularly sensitive to the movements of the 10-year Treasury yield ( ^TNX ), which has jumped to multiyear highs in recent weeks.

Unpacking what's moving bond yields higher so quickly is more complicated. Economists point to a web of factors causing investors to rewrite their expectations for inflation and economic growth.

"There's clearly a trend," said Daryl Fairweather, chief economist at Redfin. "There's something meaningful happening with us moving into a higher-for-longer economy."

While it's impossible to predict where bond yields and mortgage rates go from here, 8% loans now look like a not-so-distant possibility. Here's why experts told Yahoo Finance the current environment looks like one where rates could stay high, and even keep rising.

Mortgage rates jolted higher in the weeks after the US attacked Iran on Feb. 28 as investors fretted about rising oil prices and their implications for inflation. Although oil prices have fallen from their peaks , concern remains about how higher energy prices will reverberate across supply chains, potentially worsening inflation.

Apart from oil prices themselves, general uncertainty about the situation in Iran is also pushing rates higher, as investors want more compensation for unknown risks, said Jake Krimmel, senior economist at Realtor.com.

"The geopolitical uncertainty is a huge part of it," Krimmel said. "We're talking about supply shock. That doesn't just touch oil, but probably everything else with trade."

Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has tried to lower bond yields via buybacks to little effect, has blamed much of the rise in bond yields and mortgage rates on energy prices.

"I don't know if this conflict's going to end next week, next month, in two months, but I believe on the other side of this, energy prices will be much lower and interest rates, mortgage rates will come back down," he said on Monday .

Still, few economists think energy prices alone explain today's higher rates, because the US economy has been showing the kind of growth that typically causes bond yields and mortgage rates to rise.

articles.title: Saudi Airport Hit Again as Riyadh Set to Host Major Conferences
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia’s main airport came under renewed attack from Houthi rebels, a day after a strike on the facility killed 12 people and heaped pressure on the Mi...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Saudi Arabia's main airport came under renewed attack from Houthi rebels, a day after a strike on the facility killed 12 people and heaped pressure on the Middle East's biggest economy as it prepares to host major events that seek to boost foreign investment.

An unidentified projectile hit a passenger terminal at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Sunday, with authorities tackling a blaze, the Saudi-led coalition that's fighting Iranian-backed Houthi militants in Yemen, said in a statement. The Houthis swiftly claimed the attacks, saying they were a response to "Saudi aggression."

The Saudi civil aviation authority said that the attack resulted in injuries and that the damage was being assessed, without offering additional details. The coalition also said air defenses had intercepted a missile near the same location in the Saudi capital.

The incident follows the strike on King Khalid airport on Saturday that also injured more than 300 people and marked the deadliest single event in Saudi Arabia since the Iran war began in late February. A projectile also fell near the King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia's Dammam, which the Houthis also claimed as one of their attacks.

The blast at the Riyadh airport on Saturday brought travel at the airport to a near-standstill. It also forced the capital's financial hub to shift to remote work until further notice and prompted executives from BP Plc and Shell Plc to pull out of a major energy event in the city this week.

Authorities have indicated the 25th World Petroleum Congress and associated events, due to run from Sunday through Oct. 15, will go ahead. The city is also scheduled to host the Future Investment Initiative, Riyadh's flagship investor gathering, later this month.

The two events are set to draw industry heavyweights, including Wall Street titans such as Goldman Sachs' David Solomon and BlackRock's Larry Fink.

The FII's organizers on Sunday said they were preparing to "welcome thousands of delegates to Riyadh" for the event starting Oct. 26.

"Comprehensive security measures will be in place at Riyadh's airports, our conference venues and official hotels, with coordinated arrangements for participants' transportation and movements," the group's chief executive officer, Maha Al Saud, said in a statement.

articles.title: For the first time ever, 10-year bond yields track diesel prices more closely than crude, and Trump’s fuel deal with Putin may be too little too late
articles.summary: "Ultimately, diesel and gasoline drive inflation, not crude oil."
articles.body:
Diesel prices have come off their all-time highs in recent weeks, but the key industrial fuel has already moved the needle across the economy and financial markets, making affordability a more potent issue in the midterm elections.

The national average for diesel is about $6.277 per gallon, according to AAA , down from its $6.528 high but still 71% above year-ago levels. By contrast, U.S. crude oil is up 56% from a year earlier as damage to refining capacity in the Middle East and Russia has produced a sharper crunch in fuel markets.

Because diesel is a critical input in manufacturing, agriculture and logistics, the recent price surge has been felt broadly. The latest consumer and producer price indexes showed jumps in transportation costs, while purchasing manager surveys signaled big spikes in prices businesses are paying.

"This is why products have been trading at double the price of crude during the past few months, something that has never happened before. Ultimately, diesel and gasoline drive inflation, not crude oil," Amrita Sen, director of market intelligence and co-founder at Energy Aspects, wrote in the Financial Times on Wednesday.

And as higher fuel costs keep inflation forecasts elevated, markets are pricing in a more hawkish Federal Reserve that's ready to hike rates further. Bond yields have risen in anticipation of tighter monetary policy, raising borrowing costs for consumers.

Crude prices had previously moved in tandem with prices for refined products and had long been a proxy for those costs, but that relationship has broken down, according to Sen.

"In fact, since May, 10-year US Treasury yields have correlated more closely with diesel prices than crude prices, for the first time ever," she added.

That's why the Trump administration has started paying more attention lately to bringing down diesel prices, Sen said.

Over the past week alone, President Donald Trump has taken steps to ease the cost burden. On Monday, he signed an executive order to defer the 24-cent federal tax per gallon on diesel until the end of the year, though most states have separate levies on diesel.

And on Friday, he said he reached a deal with Vladimir Putin to obtain diesel from Russia , a stunning reversal from years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its invasion of Ukraine.

Russia will supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel now, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter," according to Trump. Russia will deliver another 3 million tons "within a short period of time" after that.

articles.title: Strip out AI stocks, and the US market lags Europe
articles.summary: If you've ever wondered what the US stock market might look like without AI, look no further than Europe.
articles.body:
If you've ever wondered what the US stock market might look like without AI, look no further than Europe.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) has gained roughly 13.5% since the start of the year, adding roughly $9 trillion in market capitalization as the tech sector's run has lifted the entire index even as other sectors have faltered.

But strip out AI-related stocks, and the picture changes. Remove those companies, and the US equity market hasn't beaten Europe — it has instead slightly lagged, as European markets have found their own strength. An index of the so-called "old economy" that removes AI-related names has gained just 5.5% since Jan. 1. Europe's STOXX 600 index ( ^STOXX ), tracking the leading 600 companies in Europe, has gained roughly 5.6% over the same period.

"The bloc has probably missed out on the AI investment boom," BNP Paribas economists James Egelhof and Andrew Husby wrote to clients.

To be clear, AI is not the whole story in the cross-Atlantic divergence.

The US was outperforming Europe before the advent of OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) ChatGPT in November 2022 and before the current capital expenditures boom. The US economy is more dynamic for reasons ranging from demographics and fiscal policy to far stronger capital markets, abundant and cheap domestic energy, and the world's most powerful and well-capitalized corporate sector.

Yet the capital expenditures boom and economic gains following the 2022 launch of ChatGPT have disproportionately accrued in the US market, flowing into US companies and investors. In other words, the AI investment boom didn't create the US advantage, but it is magnifying the US lead.

Global AI investments are expected to exceed $1 trillion this year, with expectations that the figure will grow to roughly $1.4 trillion in 2027, per research from Bank of America. Yet hardware investment, or actual construction of data centers and other AI infrastructure, remains concentrated in the US as the US and Canada account for roughly 60% of new data center capacity additions in 2026 compared to Europe's approximately 10% share, per Goldman Sachs.

Compared to Europe, the US is capturing a much larger share of the direct investment, corporate profits, and equity performance. Where the US hosts roughly three-quarters of global computing capacity, the eurozone hosts only 5%, per ECB data.

"European capital markets are smaller and more fragmented, bank-based financing can favour incumbents, and regulatory and market fragmentation can slow diffusion," Egelhof and Husby wrote. "Even in our most optimistic scenarios, the eurozone results fall short of the US."

articles.title: Massie backs Trump’s diesel deal with Russia in rare move
articles.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) on Sunday backed President Trump’s deal with Russia for diesel, in spite of past conflict between the two politicians. “In 2022 I voted against Russia sanctions, pointing out that U.S. citizens would suffer from higher prices. Glad to see Trump came around to that reality this week. We should lift sanctions…
articles.body:
Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) on Sunday backed President Trump’s deal with Russia for diesel, in spite of past conflict between the two politicians.

“In 2022 I voted against Russia sanctions, pointing out that U.S. citizens would suffer from higher prices. Glad to see Trump came around to that reality this week. We should lift sanctions on all petroleum products, and on raw metals like copper and aluminum,” Massie said in a Sunday post on the social platform X, featuring a screenshot of a Truth Social post from the president discussing the deal.

Trump announced Friday that Russia would provide the U.S. and global market with diesel. The move comes only a few weeks out from the midterm elections, in which increasing energy prices are a central issue.

The president said that Moscow would “immediately” give 300,000 tons of diesel to the U.S. and the global marketplace.

“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter,” he wrote in a post on Truth Social.

Energy prices have risen amid the U.S. war against Iran, with the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the oil industry, closed amid the conflict. According to AAA , the average price of a gallon of diesel in the U.S. was about $6.28 on Sunday afternoon, up from $3.67 last year at the same time.

Massie’s support for the Russia deal is notable, given his recent tension with the president.

The Kentucky Republican has a history of an independent streak but has increasingly broken with Trump on issues the president cares deeply about.

Massie was one of the leaders in the push for the administration to release files about convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. He also went after the GOP’s approach to foreign policy and did not vote for Trump’s signature tax and spending legislation.

articles.title: RBI measures: Rupee to gain sharply but forex liquidity likely to dry up
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Forex dealers expect a gap opening in the rupee-dollar exchange rate, with the domestic unit likely to record its sharpest gain in recent times.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Forex dealers expect a gap opening in the rupee-dollar exchange rate, with the domestic unit likely to record its sharpest gain in recent times. However, there is also a looming market freeze, with RBI's aggressive anti-speculation measures risking paralysis of legitimate market-making, choking interbank liquidity and inadvertently penalising genuine corporate hedgers.Oil companies, normally the market's largest daily dollar buyers, will source dollars through RBI's special window, while stricter documentation rules could slow other commercial purchases. Meanwhile, RBI's dollar sales and expectations of rupee appreciation may prompt holders to sell dollars, adding to downward pressure on the dollar."While the weekend measures will support the rupee in the immediate term, liquidity in the forex market could dry up very quickly. Desks need substantial operational clarity from RBI before they have the confidence to quote two-way prices again," said Ashhish Vaidya, head of treasury at DBS Bank.RBI's new 20% Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) means selling forex derivatives to an importer client now forces the bank to lock up 20% interest-free cash with RBI. Because dealers do not yet know how or when this reserve will be debited, they cannot accurately price their trades.One area where clarity is sought is cross-currency swaps, such as those used to hedge external commercial borrowings (ECBs), or coupon-only and principal-only swap structures.In a foreign currency borrowing swap, repaying the loan principal is a capital-account transaction, exempt from the 20% reserve. However, paying periodic interest on the loan is a current-account transaction.The question before banks is: "If an Indian company buys forward dollars to hedge its upcoming loan interest, does the lending bank have to park 20% cash with RBI on just the interest portion or on the entire swap contract?"Locking up 20% in idle cash with the central bank carries an opportunity cost of roughly 6.5% to 7% in lost interest. Banks will pass this direct cost on to corporates through steep swap spreads, making standard hedging uneconomical for genuine borrowers.Importers who prudently locked in forward contracts or currency futures to cover upcoming import bills are "long" on the dollar, meaning they gain if the dollar rises and incur paper losses if the rupee strengthens. If the rupee suddenly surges by more than Rs 1 against the US dollar, these long-dollar positions could incur substantial mark-to-market (MTM) losses, which the importers would have to cover."Slashing the threshold from $100 million to $5 million for derivative transactions without underlying merchant transactions creates an administrative headache. articles.title: Check your email: $15.8 million being sent to users of cash advance app, FTC says
articles.summary: More than 2 million payments are being sent out, according to the FTC.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – If you’ve used the AI-based cash advance app Cleo, you may be receiving a payment from the Federal Trade Commission soon.

The FTC announced last week that it would be sending out more than $15.8 million to users impacted by “Cleo AI’s deceptive claims about the amounts and timing of available cash advances and the company’s hard-to-cancel subscriptions.”

In a complaint filed last year, the FTC alleged Cleo misled customers about how quickly they could access cash advances and how much they would receive. The agency said Cleo suggested to customers that they could have “access to ‘hundreds of dollars’ in cash advances when almost no one received even close to the advertised amounts.”

Cleo was also accused of charging hidden fees for same-day or instant cash advances, only for the advance to take until the next day “often,” and for making it difficult for users to cancel.

In March, Cleo agreed to pay $17 million to settle the allegations.

More than 2.1 million Cleo AI customers are expected to receive payments from the FTC. Eligible users, “who paid for eligible instant cash advances,” are expected to receive an email from no-reply@consumersentinel.gov by Oct. 26, if they haven’t already.

PayPal payments are expected to follow starting on Oct. 27, the FTC said. If you receive such a payment, the FTC says you should redeem it within 30 days.

The FTC didn’t say exactly how much consumers would receive, but if the 2,124,796 payments the agency is sending out were an equal portion of the more than $15.8 million pot, each person could expect just under $7.50.

While agreeing to the settlement, Cleo did not admit any wrongdoing.

The festive season, which typically accounts for a significant share of annual smartphone sales, is expected to be driven more by replacement demand than first-time buyers."The key challenge this festive season will be the size of the active consumer pool," said Tarun Pathak, research director at Counterpoint Research. Higher smartphone prices, he said, are likely to keep many consumers on the sidelines, with discretionary upgrades being deferred and purchases increasingly driven by replacement needs.The trend is also reflected in device trade-ins, which are emerging as an important driver of premium smartphone purchases."This festive season is shaping up as an upgrade season more than a first-purchase season. Fewer people are buying a phone for the first time, but the ones who are buying are moving up," said Sreevathsa Prabhakar, founder and CEO of Servify.Servify, which handles over 3 lakh device trade-ins annually, said trade-in volumes in Oct and Nov are typically around 50% higher than in regular months.Prabhakar said upgrades in the Rs 60,000-1 lakh smartphone segment are being driven largely by financing and trade-ins. Its proposed distribution and commission reforms aim to remove incentives for mis-selling. In an interview with TOI, chairman Ajay Seth explains the changes. Excerpts:What is the intent behind the consultation paper on distribution; is it to stop mis-sellingThe intent is fourfold: expanding coverage, improving affordability, enhancing accessibility, especially in underserved areas and economic segments, and generating employment. The specific objectives are to remove regulatory arbitrage, bring more entities and persons into distribution, make the sector cost-efficient, incentivise good market conduct and enhance transparency. Addressing mis-selling is integral to this, but it is not the only driver. If you look at the structure, high upfront commission on first-year premium induces mis-selling and a high proportion of surrenders; only about 48% of life policies reach the 61st month. In credit life, a low- or nil-effort product, single-premium commissions have ranged from 22% to 57%, often alongside compulsory bundling with loans. The reforms link remuneration to effort, reward persistency, end compulsory bundling and make conduct visible through the Public Insurance Registry.Will it fully address the problem given that other competing financial products offer much lower commission?No single measure will address it fully, which is why the reforms are a package. In 2009, mutual funds changed because several things came together: distribution reforms, market infrastructure and changes in how the industry functioned. We are approaching insurance in a similarly comprehensive manner. The reforms rationalise overall expenses of management, of which commission is one part, so insurers must become efficient in both distribution and operations. Alongside, there is suitability as a real obligation; traceability of every sale to the person who solicited it; commission clawback where mis-selling is established; curbs on compulsory bundling; public disclosure of conduct through the Public Insurance Registry.The industry warns that the new norms could slow business and threaten livelihoods…Discussion is welcome but the status quo is not serving the sector either: premiums have only tracked GDP, not outpaced it, which is the need, and the number of policies has not grown enough. Livelihoods in distribution depend on how many people can enter and earn, not on how high commission rates are. The reforms widen that base through lower capital and fees, permanent registration, additional commission for smaller towns and rural areas, and freedom to sell other financial and non-financial products. Agents in closed architecture get relatively higher limits, and stronger renewal commissions let them build a lasting book of customers. As trust grows, insurance becomes easier to sell.Corporate-focused brokers argue that commission caps could undermine investments and threaten cost recovery, while the General Insurance Council cites low non-life insurance margins and smaller players fear larger insurers will benefit. How do you respond?We will consider every submission backed by sound reasoning. On corporate broking, the proposal provides for disclosure of commission on commercial policies with sum insured above Rs 50 crore. Fee-based risk management advisory can be an alternative model for brokers who add specialised value. On margins, low profitability is not an argument for higher distribution costs and that too at the cost of the policyholder. The effort should always be oriented towards enhancing policyholder value and improving service. We have proposed the EoM level at which the sector was operating in the recent past. Recovering efficiency is how margins improve. On size, commission caps benefit all players — new and small included. They remove the leeway larger insurers have to outbid others for distribution, so insurers compete on products, pricing and service, and distribution networks are not poached by the highest bidder. New companies will continue to get flexibility in their first five years.General insurers have proposed a mandatory co-pay on health insurance. Will that not be unfair for customers willing to pay for a high sum insured and will it not defeat the purpose of buying insurance to avoid keeping an emergency health fund?We have not yet received any such proposal. When it is proposed by the industry players, we will examine the suggestion. Co-payment has a role when the customer chooses it in exchange for a lower premium, and such options already exist. But the purpose of health insurance is financial protection at the time of need. Any design that shifts costs to policyholders must be weighed against that purpose, especially for those willing to pay for higher cover. Before the burden moves to customers, the system's own inefficiencies need attention. In some cases, insurers pay only around Rs 67 in claims for every Rs 100 of premium, and distribution and operating costs have risen sharply. That is where the first correction must come. Product design will be taken up comprehensively in the product reforms planned for FY28.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Risks Rupture With Trump as Midterms Pressure Mounts
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is on a collision course with President Donald Trump, who is increasingly looking at Kyiv’s battle against Russia pri...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is on a collision course with President Donald Trump, who is increasingly looking at Kyiv's battle against Russia primarily through the lens of energy prices ahead of US midterm elections.

Trump sprung an announcement of an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine on Zelenskyy, as the US leader pushes for him to stop bombing Russian oil refineries and defends a controversial deal with Vladimir Putin on diesel exports.

After Trump posted on social media about the ceasefire, Zelenskyy said he is willing to accept it, but only if Russia does too — his long-standing position — making clear his significant doubts about that prospect.

"Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well," Zelenskyy said on social media, adding that he is "awaiting details" from the US on the deal.

But as Ukraine continues to respond to Russia's invasion with its own attacks on refineries, Zelenskyy increasingly risks running afoul of Trump. That poses a hazard for Kyiv as it still relies on US weapon purchases that are financed by other NATO allies and on intelligence-sharing from Washington. Ukraine is also strapped for cash ahead of the fifth winter of the war.

A day before his ceasefire announcement — the second in as many months — Trump lashed out at Zelenskyy, suggesting he should consider stepping aside as Ukraine's president. On Friday, after Trump reached the diesel export deal with Putin, Ukrainian negotiators cut short their talks in Miami with US envoys, according to people familiar with the matter, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly.

In the meeting, US negotiators, led by Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, told Ukrainian officials that the US was a strong partner, providing munitions and intelligence, and so Ukraine shouldn't take actions that hurt American consumers like striking refineries, according to one of the people. That was perceived as an implied threat from the US to cut off intelligence to Kyiv, several of the people said. The Financial Times was first to report about the intelligence cutoff remark at the Miami meeting.

In 2026, the stock market will observe 10 holidays, including two early closings. Many stock market holidays are also federal holidays and banking holidays.

The U.S. stock market's regular hours are 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Eastern time, Monday through Friday. The two major U.S. stock exchanges, the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the Nasdaq, each observe these trading hours. Both stock exchanges are closed on weekends.

You can still place orders to buy and sell stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) during extended trading hours, but there is added risk. The trading volume is lighter after hours, so prices can be more volatile, and your orders may not execute fully.

If you ever find yourself wondering, "Is the stock market open today?" check out this list of stock market holidays for 2026 and 2027.

Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day: Monday, Jan. 19

Most American financial markets also close for a National Day of Mourning upon the death of a past or sitting president. Typically, this day is observed on the day the funeral is held.

articles.title: Firmus Fiasco Wipes Out $700 Million of Early Backer Maas’ Value
articles.summary: Maas Group Holdings Ltd. has lost more than A$1 billion ($699 million) in market value as Firmus Grid Ltd.’s initial public offering unraveled, with the shar...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Maas Group Holdings Ltd. has lost more than A$1 billion ($699 million) in market value as Firmus Grid Ltd.'s initial public offering unraveled, with the shares extending their decline to a fifth day after Jefferies Financial Group Inc. downgraded its rating.

Shares of the Australian construction company dropped as much as 14% Monday, taking their five-day decline to 42%. Analysts at Jefferies cut their recommendation on the stock to hold from buy and lowered earnings forecasts, citing heightened uncertainty from the failed Firmus IPO.

Maas Group, which is both an investor and contractor for Firmus, has become a proxy for the data center operator in the last week as its efforts to raise as much as $5.5 billion collapsed. The company builds modular power cubes for Firmus through its JLE unit and reaffirmed its expectations to complete work orders by the end of 2027. It held a 3.2% interest in Firmus as of August.

"In our view, risks have amplified," wrote Jefferies analysts led by John Campbell in a note. The IPO failure is a "highly impactful" event for Maas across both its earnings and equity investment in Firmus, increasing concerns of a slower rollout, they added.

Jefferies also lowered its price target on the stock to A$4.85 apiece from A$7 and reduced its earnings and revenue estimates for the fiscal years through 2029. The broker also slashed the assumed value of Maas Group's Firmus stake to A$300 million from A$410 million.

Firmus is exploring options to raise as much as $3 billion in a private funding round after pulling its IPO plans, people familiar with the matter have said. It abandoned its Australian listing application on Friday as demand from offshore investors dried up for what would have been one of Australia's largest ever debuts.

articles.title: Five Bangalore landowners faced tax on rental income from an IT park built through a partnership firm; IT department alleged it was a tax-avoidance structure, ITAT gives relief
articles.summary: What constitutes tax avoidance?
articles.body: What constitutes tax avoidance? In a recent ruling, five Bangalore landowners have secured relief from ITAT in an income tax dispute over alleged undisclosed rental income.They established that the building belonged to their partnership firm, which received rent directly into its bank account, filed income tax returns and paid taxes on the earnings.What the case is aboutIn 1999, five landowners decided to develop their property into an IT park and SEZ zone. To take the project forward, they signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with a builder.Also Read | He bought a Rs 41.85 lakh and paid Rs 39.15 lakh but did not get possession; builder blames PMC-PMRDA jurisdiction changes, MahaRERA rejects excuse and orders interest payout to homebuyerIn 2005, the landowners and the same builder executed a registered joint development agreement (JDA). Under the arrangement, the builder was granted development rights and a Power of Attorney (POA) was executed for various purposes. The builder also paid the landowners a refundable, interest-free deposit of Rs 37.25 lakh.As part of the development, the builder was to construct a separate C1 Block for SEZ activities. He subsequently set up a partnership firm to manage the block, retaining a 96% stake while the landowners collectively held the remaining 4%.Once the construction was completed, the firm leased the premises to several companies. The rental payments were credited directly to its bank account.The partnership firm also filed its income tax returns and paid tax on its earnings. Meanwhile, the landowners made withdrawals from the firm in the usual course.The C1 Block was constructed and allotted to the landowners in AY 2016-17. They also paid the BBMP tax relating to the block.The arrangement continued without any apparent dispute until 2022, when the Income Tax Department conducted a search at a company associated with the landowners' family. The findings from the operation triggered a series of disputes.Also Read | Man invested Rs 10 lakh, which tax department treated as unexplained; he first cited cash loan, then bank withdrawals as source, ITAT Nagpur deletes addition and Rs 2.11 lakh penaltyAt the centre of the tax controversy was the commercial property in Block C1, developed under the 2005 JDA.The Assessing Officer (AO) of the Income Tax Department took the position that the landowners, rather than the partnership firm, were the property's actual owners.The AO consequently viewed the firm as an arrangement designed to evade tax, maintaining that the landowners were the real owners of Block C1.The AO cited, among other reasons, withdrawals made by the landowner families that were not proportionate to their declared 4% profit-sharing entitlement. The officer also alleged that the partnership deed had not been registered.On this basis, the AO sought to assess the rental earnings from Block C1 directly in the hands of the landowners and their family members, instead of the partnership firm. The Commissioner of Appeals (CIT(A)) agreed with this position and upheld the assessment approach.The landowners subsequently challenged the decision before the Bangalore bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) and won relief.Also Read | Landlords wanted tenant out to open a law office; he said the reason for seeking eviction had changed and other properties were available, why Delhi High Court upheld evictionWhy did the landowners win the case?Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that the ITAT Bangalore relied on substantial documentary evidence to establish that the partnership firm was a genuine business entity.Government and statutory authorities had recognised it as a co-developer of the SEZ, while infrastructure and electricity approvals were issued in its name. Its audited financial statements also reflected the rental earnings, and tenants paid rent directly into the firm's bank account.Surana highlighted that the Income-tax Department had itself assessed the partnership firm in previous years and accepted the rental income reported in its returns.The tribunal also dismissed the department's contention that withdrawals made by the landowner partners established that the rental earnings had actually accrued to them personally.According to the ITAT Bangalore, amounts taken out by partners are ordinarily entered in the partnership firm's books as debits to their respective capital accounts.Surana says: “Such withdrawals do not, merely for that reason, become fresh rental income in the partners' hands, nor do they transfer ownership of the underlying property from the firm to the partners.”Also Read | Woman buys Rs 1.03 crore 3BHK in Bengaluru, but builder fails to provide specially-enabled parking; Karnataka RERA orders provision within 60 days and audited maintenance accountsThe tribunal further pointed out that one of the taxpayers involved in the dispute was not a partner in the firm at all and had received no money from it.Separately, the ITAT examined the capital gains issue arising from the JDA. The Assessing Officer (AO) had proposed taxing the gains in AY 2016-17, arguing that the builder had completed the construction and handed over the developed area to the landowners during that year.The landowners maintained that the taxable transfer had taken place much earlier, when they signed the registered JDA and executed the Power of Attorney in March 2005, thereby placing effective control of the property with the builder.On examining the agreement, the tribunal found that the developer had been granted extensive and irrevocable rights from the beginning. These included access to the property, securing approvals, designing and developing the project, signing agreements with purchasers and mortgaging the property to arrange finance. The registered Power of Attorney (POA) had also vested broad authority in the developer.Based on these provisions, the ITAT Bangalore concluded that the transfer had already taken place in AY 2005-06, around the time the JDA and POA were executed. Consequently, the transfer could not be treated as having occurred in AY 2016-17 merely because the completed area was handed over to the landowners during that year.Ultimately, the taxpayers succeeded in all their appeals, with the disputed additions being deleted. The landowners secured the favourable ruling from the Bangalore ITAT on August 27, 2026.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Oil prices today: Brent crude declines as Trump announces Russia-Ukraine energy truce
articles.summary: Oil prices fell on Monday as expectations of additional Russian diesel supplies and a possible halt to attacks on energy facilities in the Russia-Ukraine
articles.body: Oil prices fell on Monday as expectations of additional Russian diesel supplies and a possible halt to attacks on energy facilities in the Russia-Ukraine conflict eased some concerns over supply. However, continued tensions in the Middle East kept Brent crude above $100 a barrel.Brent crude futures fell $1.54, or 1.47%, to $103.18 a barrel by 7.24 am IST. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude declined by the same amount, or 1.68%, to $90.31 a barrel.ICE gasoil futures, a benchmark for diesel, fell 3% to $1,436 per barrel after US President Donald Trump said Russia would supply additional diesel to US and global markets.Earlier on Friday, Trump said that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel, equivalent to around 2.25 million barrels.He added that another 500,000 tonnes would be supplied in November, followed by a further 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.Global daily diesel consumption is forecast to be close to 29 million barrels, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA).Trump also announced on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other’s energy facilities. However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he was still waiting for details of the proposed energy ceasefire.The announcements eased some immediate concerns over supply, said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade, Reuters reported.“Questions remain over the validity and longevity of any such ceasefire, and without clearer evidence that it will actually hold, the extent of the pullback is likely to stay limited,” he added.Despite the easing of some supply concerns, the conflict in the Middle East continued to support oil prices. The Houthis claimed responsibility for a Saturday strike on Riyadh's international airport that reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300.Saudi authorities also reported injuries in another attack on the airport on Sunday.Trump said on Saturday that the US was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis. The conflict has spilled over from the wider war involving Iran, launched by the US and Israel in February.Attacks on tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz have also increased this month, threatening to disrupt the recovery in Middle Eastern crude exports seen in September.Goldman Sachs raised its Brent crude price forecast for December to $90 a barrel from $85, according to a note by analysts led by Daan Struyven.“We maintain our base case that continued adaptation of Mideast supply will eventually reduce crude oil prices, while potential renewed escalation still poses significant net upside risk,” the analysts said, estimating a risk premium of just over $20 a barrel.“We forecast WTI prices, which are unusually low vs Brent because of high US-Europe shipping costs, to average $81 in December 2026 and $73 in 2027,” they added.Oil prices ended the previous week with mixed movements. Brent futures for December delivery rose $2.47, or 2.41%, to $104.72 a barrel, while WTI gained 1% to settle at $91.85 a barrel.With Brent crude trading above $100 a barrel, geopolitical developments are likely to remain a key driver of prices. Progress in US-Iran negotiations could ease pressure, but the risk of renewed attacks, shipping disruptions and prolonged supply constraints is expected to keep volatility elevated.You use AI every day. articles.title: Elon Musk y la 'nueva' moneda mundial: "Es la mejor métrica para la verdadera fuerza de cualquier economía"
articles.standfirst: El magnate reflexiona sobre el denominador común de los países más ricos
articles.summary: El magnate reflexiona sobre el denominador común de los países más ricos
articles.body: No son las reservas de oro ni el PIB. Tampoco el músculo militar o las tierras raras. Para Elon Musk, el hombre más rico del mundo según la revista Forbes, actualmente la nueva moneda que determina qué país es más potente es otra. "La producción de electricidad es la mejor métrica para la verdadera fuerza de cualquier economía a gran escala, en mi opinión", ha afirmado el CEO de Tesla, SpaceX o X en su propia red social, acumulando millones de visualizaciones. Elon Musk ha citado un gráfico en el que se cruzan los datos del consumo de electricidad per cápita con el PIB per cápita de los distintos países del mundo. La conclusión, según esta información basada en los registros del 2021 del Banco Mundial, es contundente: no hay territorios ricos que consuman cantidades bajas de electricidad. En la parte baja del cuadro encontramos países como Somalia, Burundi, Tanzania o Nigeria, entre muchos otros. En la superior, Noruega, Estados Unidos, Reino Unido... Pat Gelsinger, ex CEO de Intel, ha afirmado en declaraciones recogidas por a16z que la generación de energía en Estados Unidos puede ser el verdadero cuello de botella para el desarrollo de la Inteligencia Artificial en el futuro. "La capacidad energética en cierto modo atenúa lo eufóricos que podemos ponernos con la IA. ¿Por qué construir un nuevo centro de datos y comprar el millón de GPUs si no puedo alimentarlos?", ha preguntado el exdirectivo de Intel. La reflexión de Pat Gelsinger va en la misma línea que la publicación de Elon Musk al señalar que la capacidad energética es la verdadera capacidad económica. Por otra parte, el antiguo CEO de Intel, muy reconocido en la industria, ha ensalzado la importancia de la energía nuclear y también ha lamentado que Estados Unidos, en cuanto a fuentes renovables, tenga una gran dependencia de China.
